info.title: freehire API
info.description:
## Base URL

The public job-search API is served under the base URL above. Catalogue reads do not require an account.

## Response envelope

Single items use a `data` envelope. Collections include pagination metadata; errors use `{ "error": "message" }` with a matching HTTP status.

```json
{ "data": { "...": "single item" } }

{ "data": [ ... ], "meta": { "total": 4213, "limit": 20, "offset": 0 } }

{ "error": "job not found" }
```

## Pagination

List and search endpoints accept limit and offset. Each endpoint documents its defaults, caps, and paging bounds; meta.total reports the matches before paging.

## Errors

Errors use standard HTTP status codes, including 400 for invalid input, 404 when a job or company is not found, 429 when rate-limited, and 503 when search is unavailable.

## Rate limits

Public reads are rate-limited. Requests over the applicable limit receive HTTP 429; honor Retry-After when it is present.

## Filtering jobs

Except where noted below, these parameters apply to `GET /jobs/search` and `GET /jobs/facets`. Combine any of them with full-text `q`.

- Pass multiple values as a comma-separated list to OR them: `skills=go,rust` matches either. Repeating the param (`skills=go&skills=rust`) also works.
- Add `<param>_mode=and` to require all selected values: `skills=go,rust&skills_mode=and` matches both.
- Add `<param>_exclude=<value>` to exclude matches: `company_type_exclude=outstaff` drops outstaff jobs.
- Different facets are ANDed together; numeric and boolean filters are ANDed too. The geography facets are the one exception — see below.
- Geography is a single OR group: `regions`, `countries`, `metros` and `cities` widen each other instead of narrowing. `regions=eu&countries=IT` means "in Europe **or** in Italy", so it returns everything `regions=eu` alone would. To search one country, drop the region: `countries=IT`. The four name a single concept — *where* — so picking two places reads as "either", which is what makes `regions=eu&countries=BR` ("Europe or Brazil") useful. There is no AND to switch on: `_mode=and` does not apply to geography.
- Use `regions=none` to match jobs with no resolved geography (an empty region set); it ORs with real region values and supports `_exclude` like any region.
- A param no filter reads is ignored rather than refused, so existing links keep working, and comes back in `meta.ignored_params`, with `did_you_mean` when it is only the singular of a real facet. Check it: a dropped filter otherwise looks like a genuinely broad result. At most 10 are listed per response. The same report rides on `/jobs/facets` and `/companies`, which grow a `meta` block only when there is something to warn about. `/companies` filters on its own vocabulary, so a jobs facet sent there is reported as ignored.

### Facets

Every facet below supports repeat-OR, `_mode=and`, and `_exclude` as described above.

| Param | Filter | Values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `collections` | Collection | yc, techstars, a16z-portfolio, a16z-speedrun, sequoia, accel, greylock, usv, bond, lightspeed, index-ventures, softbank-vision-fund, founders-fund, european, ai, mag7, bigtech, unicorn, fortune500, eastern-roots, indian-roots, ai-native, uk-skilled-worker-sponsor, nl-recognised-sponsor, us-h1b-sponsor, ca-lmia-employer, ie-permit-employer, dk-fast-track-company |
| `regions` | Region | global, north_america, latam, eu, uk, mena, africa, apac, cis, none |
| `work_mode` | Work format | remote, hybrid, onsite |
| `category` | Specialization | software_engineering, backend, frontend, fullstack, mobile, devops, sre, network_engineering, it_support, data_engineering, data_science, data_analytics, ml_ai, ai_engineering, qa, security, hardware, embedded, blockchain, architecture, design, creative, engineering_design, industrial_engineering, occupational_safety, product, project_management, healthcare, skilled_trades, retail, hospitality, logistics, education, personal_services, administration, social_services, science, manufacturing, public_safety, marketing, sales, support, business_analysis, solutions_engineering, developer_relations, technical_writing, recruiting, hr, finance, legal, operations, customer_success, other. The retired value management is still accepted and answered as role_type=people_manager |
| `ai_archetype` | AI Specialization | rag_app_builder, agent_builder, cloud_ml_platform_engineer, ml_trainer_researcher, fullstack_ai_engineer, devops_infra_engineer |
| `seniority` | Seniority | intern, junior, middle, senior, lead, staff, principal, c_level |
| `role_type` | Role type | people_manager — the title names a people-management role. One value only: carrying nothing means no management marker was found, NOT that the posting is individual-contributor work, so role_type_exclude means "no marker", not "IC" |
| `skills` | Skills | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |
| `domains` | Industry | fintech, crypto, ecommerce, gambling, gamedev, media, travel, healthcare, edtech, govtech, devtools, cybersecurity, ai, hrtech, adtech, proptech, logistics, mobility, climatetech, other |
| `company_type` | Company type | product, startup, outsource, outstaff, agency, inhouse, government |
| `countries` | Countries | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |
| `cities` | City | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values. Recognized dictionary aliases such as München and Köln resolve to their canonical city names. |
| `metros` | Metro area | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |
| `relocation` | Relocation | not_supported, supported, required |
| `employment_type` | Employment | full_time, part_time, contract, internship, fellowship |
| `engagement` | Contract terms | ir35_outside, ir35_inside, w2, 1099, c2c, contract_to_hire, b2b, uop, umowa_zlecenie, umowa_o_dzielo, clt, pj, tk, gph, samozanyaty, ip, freiberuflich, arbeitnehmerueberlassung, zzp, auto_entrepreneur, portage_salarial, autonomo, monotributo — employee or own business, in each market's own term (UK IR35, US W-2/1099/C2C, Polish B2B and umowy, Brazilian CLT/PJ, Russian ТК/ГПХ/самозанятость/ИП, German, Dutch, French, Spanish and Argentine freelance statuses), as the title, the description or a source's own contract-type field states it; a posting offering several carries each, one that does not say carries none. Separate from employment_type |
| `english_level` | English | none, a1, a2, b1, b2, c1, c2, native |
| `posting_language` | Job language | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |
| `reality` | Posting reality | fresh, stale, likely-evergreen |
| `salary_currency` | Currency | USD, EUR, GBP, RUB |
| `perks` | Perks mentioned | generous_pto, four_day_week, 401k_match, parental_leave, retirement_plan, tuition_reimbursement, unlimited_pto, health_insurance, mental_health, learning_budget, home_office_stipend, sabbatical, sign_on_bonus — matched from the description; a posting without one does not mention it, which is not the same as not offering it |
| `equity` | Equity | salary_and_equity, equity_only, not_stated — not_stated means none was read, not that the job offers no equity |
| `company_slug` | Company | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |
| `source_type` | Source type | ats, company, aggregator, social |
| `clearance_levels` | Clearance level | none, confidential, secret, top_secret, ts_sci, public_trust, interim, other. none = no detected clearance requirement (the same postings as requires_clearance=false); other = a non-US scheme (UK SC/DV, AU NV1, NATO) or a clearance stated with no level; interim is stated beside a level, not instead of one |
| `source` | Source | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |
| `company_size` | Company size | 1-10, 11-50, 51-200, 201-500, 501-1000, 1000+ |
| `education_level` | Education level | none, bachelor, master, phd |
| `salary_period` | Salary period | year, month, day, hour |

### Numeric & boolean filters

| Param | Filter | Values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `visa_sponsorship` | Visa sponsorship | true, false |
| `requires_clearance` | Security clearance required | true, false |
| `via_recruiter` | Posting says a recruiter publishes it for a client | true — the description says so; false — every posting not marked, including recruiter posts that never say so |
| `salary_min` | Minimum salary | integer — jobs whose minimum salary is at least this (pair with salary_currency) |
| `salary_max` | Maximum salary | integer — jobs whose maximum salary is at most this (pair with salary_currency) |
| `experience_years_min` | Minimum experience | integer — jobs requiring at least this many years |
| `experience_years_max` | Maximum experience | integer — jobs requiring at most this many years, the same figure experience_years_min bounds from below. Use 0 for jobs stating no prior experience is required. Either bound excludes jobs that state no requirement at all, unless experience_include_unspecified is set |
| `experience_include_unspecified` | Include unstated experience | true — with either experience bound, also keep the jobs that state no experience requirement (most of the catalogue). Has no effect without a bound |
| `experience_only_seniority_unspecified` | Experience only without a level | true — apply either experience bound only to the jobs that carry no seniority level; a job with a level passes the bound whatever it states. With seniority and seniority_include_unspecified this reads "one of these levels, or no level and within the bound". Has no effect without a bound |
| `seniority_include_unspecified` | Include unstated seniority | true — with seniority, also keep the jobs that carry no seniority level (most of the catalogue). Has no effect without an included seniority |
| `posted_within_days` | Posted within | integer — jobs whose SOURCE states a posting date in the last N days. Some boards restate that date on every crawl, so a job open for months can satisfy a narrow bound here; open_within_days is the one that cannot be rewritten from outside |
| `open_within_days` | Open within | integer — jobs first recorded by freehire in the last N days, i.e. how long the posting has been in the catalogue regardless of the date its source states. Independent of posted_within_days; both may be set and they narrow together |

### Recipes

- **Senior Go, remote, in the CIS region** — `q=go&seniority=senior&work_mode=remote&regions=cis`
- **Backend roles, freshest first, in Germany** — `category=backend&countries=DE&sort=posted_at&order=desc`
- **One country only — no region param, or it widens back out** — `countries=IT&employment_type=contract`
- **Must use both Go and Rust** — `skills=go,rust&skills_mode=and`
- **Exclude outstaff companies** — `company_type_exclude=outstaff`
- **At least $100k, with visa sponsorship** — `salary_currency=USD&salary_min=100000&visa_sponsorship=true`
- **Excluding jobs that need a security clearance** — `clearance_levels=none`
- **Jobs stating Secret or Top Secret clearance** — `clearance_levels=secret,top_secret`
- **Only jobs that need a security clearance** — `requires_clearance=true`

get.summary: List jobs, newest first, with limit/offset pagination.
get.description: Takes no filters at all — `limit` and `offset` are the whole vocabulary. Anything else is ignored rather than refused, and listed in `meta.ignored_params`: a filter param sent here returns the entire catalogue, which is indistinguishable from a narrow result unless you check. Use `/jobs/search` to filter.

get.summary: Full-text + faceted search over open jobs.
get.description:
Combine free-text `q` with any of the filter params below. Repeated facet params are ORed; add `<param>_mode=and` to require all, or `<param>_exclude=<value>` to exclude. Without `q`, results default to newest first; with `q`, to relevance. A param no filter reads is ignored rather than refused, and listed in `meta.ignored_params` — check it, since a dropped filter otherwise looks like a broad result.

Plus every filter in the "Filtering jobs" section above.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Full-text query over `title`, `company`, `description`, and `location`. Plain words use the default engine matching: the first words are required and trailing ones are dropped when too few postings match, so word order can change the result. Operators: quotes (`"systems engineer"`) require every quoted word in any order (not a contiguous phrase); `-word` excludes; uppercase `OR` between words matches any alternative (at most 5, merged and deduplicated); `title:` at the start of an alternative matches it in the title only, e.g. `title:"product owner" -junior OR title:produktchef`. Narrow the fields of the other alternatives with `q_fields`. Exact-phrase matching is not offered, and default relevance order does not reliably rank a contiguous match above a scattered-token one.

parameters.name: q_fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated subset of `title,company,description,location` to restrict `q` to, e.g. `title`. A name outside that set drops the whole parameter (reported in `meta.ignored_params`) rather than partially applying.

get.summary: Count of matching jobs per facet value (and numeric stats).
get.description:
Takes the same `q` and facet filter params as search, but returns the distribution of values instead of a page of jobs — use it to build filter UIs or see how a filter narrows the set. Continuous numeric facets are returned as `stats` (min/max), not per-value buckets.

Any supported search filter param narrows the counted set. (e.g. `work_mode=remote`)

get.summary: A single job by its public slug (serves closed jobs too).
Similar jobs within the same location and specialization.
get.description: Searches the live Meilisearch index with the source job’s known location and specialization as mandatory filters. Uses stored-vector hybrid ranking when available, falling back to keyword search under the same filters. Returns an empty list when location or specialization is unknown or no visible matches remain.

get.summary: Other open postings in the same role cluster (per-city duplicates).
get.description: The per-city openings folded under one canonical card by content-dedup — each keeps its own `location` and `apply_url` so a seeker picks their city. The anchor job itself is included. `meta.total` is the whole cluster size, so it stays accurate when the list is a capped page.

get.summary: List companies with job counts and denormalized facets; optional filters.
get.description: Most active first. Facet params are repeatable and filter by array overlap (OR within a facet, AND across facets), composably with `q`. `meta.total` reports the count matching the full filter.

parameters.name: regions
parameters.description: Region the company hires in. Repeatable.

parameters.name: industries
parameters.description: Curated industry. Matches a company through its curated industries **or** the equivalent job-derived domain. Repeatable.

parameters.name: domains
parameters.description: Raw job-derived domain, including values no industry names (`other`, `media`, `mobility`). Repeatable.

get.summary: Distinct company subindustry vocabulary with company counts.
get.description: Backs the searchable “Industry” facet’s option list, most common first. Counts are unconditional (they do not reflect other active list filters).

get.summary: A company and a page of its open jobs.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size for the jobs list.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Rows to skip in the jobs list.

get.summary: How one company hires over time — the company page’s Hiring tab.
get.description: The company’s postings added vs. removed per period (dense, missing periods are 0, same window rules as `/stats/jobs-activity`), its open postings now and 30 days ago, and the median days its postings stay open before an employer-side closure over the last 180 days, and the page views its postings drew over the last 30 days and the 30 before (`views`, `views_prev`: one visitor counted once per posting per day, crawlers excluded). `lifetime` is omitted below 5 such closures — absent, never 0. An unknown slug is a `404`; a slug retired by a company merge redirects `301` to the canonical one.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start date (UTC). Defaults to a per-granularity window before `to`.

get.summary: A company’s closed postings — the company page’s Closed tab.
get.description: A page of the postings the company has closed, most recently closed first. Closed postings are not in search, so this is the only list of them. There is no total: `meta.has_more` says whether another page follows. Paging reaches the first 2000 rows (`offset + limit` ≤ 2000); a deeper page is a `400`. An unknown slug is a `404`; a slug retired by a company merge redirects `301` to the canonical one.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Rows to skip; `offset + limit` may not exceed 2000.

get.summary: Prefix-search city names for autocomplete.
get.description: Population-ranked prefix search over the embedded city dictionary, optionally narrowed to one country. A blank `q` returns an empty list.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code to narrow to.

get.summary: Complete a partially typed job or company query.
get.description: Returns at most 20 suggestions. An empty query returns an empty list.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum results, default 5 and capped at 20.

get.summary: Stream recent catalogue activity using Server-Sent Events.
get.description: Replays the current feed backlog on connect, then sends new entries and periodic ping events. The connection remains open until the client disconnects.

get.summary: The headline catalogue-scale figures (open jobs, companies, sources, …).
get.description: The canonical numbers behind every "how big is this" figure on the site (the jobs list total, the /about and /open pages). Backed by one snapshot `cmd/rollup-stats` republishes periodically, not a live count. `exact: false` means the cache was cold and the figures fell back to a planner estimate — treat them as approximate when it is false.

get.summary: Return one page of job sitemap entries.
get.description: Page size and offset are bounded; defaults to 10,000 entries.

get.summary: Return a newest-first page of job sitemap entries.
get.description: The newest-job window is bounded; requests beyond it return an empty page.

get.summary: List offsets for job sitemap chunks.
get.description: The chunk size is clamped to the supported range.

get.summary: Return one page of company sitemap entries.
get.description: Page size and offset are bounded; defaults to 10,000 entries.

get.summary: List offsets for company sitemap chunks.
get.description: The chunk size is clamped to the supported range.
